An Efficient Au-Catalyzed Synthesis of Isomukonidine, Clausine L, 
Mukonidine, Glycosinine, Mukonal, and Clausine V from Propadienyl 
Methyl Ether 
Youai Qiu, Dengke Ma, Chunling Fu,* and Shengming Ma* 
Received (in XXX, XXX) Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX, Accepted Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX 5 
DOI: 10.1039/b000000x 
Naturally occurring carbazole alkaloids such as isomukonidine, clausine L, mukonidine, glycosinine, mukonal, and clausine V have been 
synthesized through a goldAcatalyzed cyclization reaction of 1A(indolA2Ayl)A2AmethoxyA2,3Aallenols, which are readily available from 
indolecarbaldehydes and methoxypropadiene. Compared to the reported procedures, our approach is general, atom economic, highly 
selective, and the starting materials are easily available.  10 
Introduction 
Carbazole alkaloids have received considerable inte rest because 
of their existence in nature and unnatural compound s with 
promising biological activities. For example, many 2Aoxygenated 
carbazole alkaloids have been isolated from differe nt parts of 15 
Murraya , which grows in southern Asia. Some of these 
compounds (Fig. 1) show useful biological activitie s:1 Mukonal 
was isolated from the stem bark of this plant by Bh attacharyya in 
1984;2 Wu and coAworkers described the isolation of mukonidine 
and its OAmethyl derivative (clausine L) from Chinese medicinal 20 
plant Clausena excavate  during studies on antiplatelet 
aggregation activity in 1993. 3 Chakraborty et al. isolated 
mukonidine from the stem bark of Murraya koenigii  in 1978, 4 
however, the physical and spectroscopic data were n ot in full 
agreement with those of Wu’s synthesized sample. Fi nally, the 25 
data of Knölker’s synthetic mukonidine confirmed th at the 
structure of Wu’s mukonidine is correct; 5 Bhattacharyya et al. 
obtained clausine L from the stem bark of Murraya koenigii  in 
1994;6 Lange et al. reported the isolation of OAmethylmukonal 
from Murraya siamensis  in 1990. 7a  Two years later, 30 
Bhattacharyya and coAworkers also obtained OAmethylmukonal 
from the root bark of a different natural source, Glycosmis 
pentaphylla  collected in Thailand, and named glycosinine. 7b  
Glycosinine was also isolated by Kongkathip and coA workers 
from the rhizomes and roots of Claysena excavate , and shows 35 
interesting antiAHIV activity; 7c  in 1999, Wu and coAworkers 
reported the isolation of clausine V from the aceto ne extract of 
the root bark of Clausena excavate.8

Knölker et al. reported the synthesis of mukonidine  based on 
the oxidation of the tricarbonyl [ η4A4a,9aAdihydroA9HAcarbazole] 
iron complex with pAchloranil (tetrachloroA1,4Abenzoquinone) 55 
providing the desired product in very low yield (22 %) together 
with the undesired 21% biaryl derivative; 9 the same group 
subsequently described a remarkable approach for th e preparation 
of clausine L, mukonidine, glycosinine, and clausin e V via  
palladium( Ⅱ)Acatalyzed oxidative cyclization of N, N A60 
diarylamines, which was prepared via  BuchwaldAHartwig 
coupling of iodobenzene and 3AmethoxyA4Amethylanili ne. 5a  
However, large amounts of oxidants (2.5 equiv of Cu (OAc) 2, 2.2 
equiv of DDQ, 25 equiv of MnO 2) and highly toxic reagent (5 
equiv of KCN) limit large scale synthesis. In the s ame year, 65 
clausine L and mukonidine were synthesized by an im proved 
palladium( Ⅱ)Acatalyzed route via  CAH activation of N,NA
diarylamines, which was synthesized by palladium(0) Acatalyzed 
BuchwaldAHartwig amination of iodobenzene and methy l 4A
aminoA2Amethoxybenzoate. 5b  Even before the isolation of the 70 
naturally occurring clausine V, Hsieh and Litt repo rted the 
synthesis of this compound via Cadogan’s reductive cyclization 
of 2Anitrobiphenyl derivative with triethyl phosphi te. 10a  In

prepared by Keuethe and Childers. The difference is  that the 2A
nitrobiphenyl derivative was synthesized by SuzukiA Miyaura 
crossAcoupling of the 4AmethoxyA2Anitrobenzenediazo nium 
tetrafluoroborate salt with 4Amethoxyphenylboronic acid. 10b  5 
However, this approach was not environmentalAfriend ly due to 
the employment of large amounts of organophosphorou s reagents 
yielding two equivalents of phosphorous oxide. Thus , a general 
and efficient route to these compounds is still des irable. In 2009, 
we have described an approach to the carbazole skel eton through 10 
a PtAcatalyzed cyclization of 1A(indolA2Ayl)A2,3Aallenols. 11  Two 
years later, we developed an AuAcatalyzed route to 2Aoxygenated 
carbazoles, which was applied to the synthesis of n aturally 
occurring carbazole alkaloids such as siamenol, cla usineAN, 
clausineAC, clauszolineAK, and clausineAM. 12  Herein, we wish to 15 
report further application of this methodology to t he general 
synthesis of isomukonidine, clausine L, mukonidine,  glycosinine, 
mukonal, and clausine V. 
Results and discussion 
By retrosynthetic analysis of these carbazoles, the  goldA
20

for synthesis of these natural carbazoles. Firstly,  we considered 
that using readily available methoxypropadiene 13  and indoleA2A
carbaldehyde as the starting materials for the synt hesis of indolyA
2,3Aallenols. 12 Then, regioselective bromination at CA3 with NA25 
bromosuccinimide, debenzylation, and necessary fina l 
transformations would afford these natural carbazol es listed in

synthesis of glycosinine, deprotonation of 5a with potassium 
hydride, bromideAlithium exchange and addition of 
dimethylformamide afforded glycosinine in 60% yield . Mukonal 
was afforded by demethylation with treatment of BBr
3 in CH 2Cl 2.

A similar approach may also be used for the synthes is of 
allenol 2b , which undergoes a smoothly AuClAcatalyzed 
cyclization under the standard reaction conditions to afford 
exclusively carbazole  3b in 74% yield from 1b  to 3b . Then, 60 
clausine V  was obtained by deprotection of the NAbenzyl group 
with potassium tertAbutoxide in dimethylsulfoxide under oxygen 
atmosphere (Scheme 3).  
 
 65 
 
Total yields of naturally occurring carbazole alkal oids from the 
readily available methoxypropadiene are: isomukonid ine (5 steps 
with 29% overall yield), clausine L (6 steps with 2 6% overall 
yield), mukonidine (7 steps with 17% overall yield) , glycosinine 70 
(5 steps with 34% overall yield), mukonal (6 steps with 30% 
overall yield), clausine V (3 steps with 61% overal l yield). The 
spectroscopic data of our synthetic compounds are i n full 
agreement with those reported for the corresponding  natural 
products. 75 
Conclusions 
In conclusion, we have realized the highly efficien t synthesis 
of isomukonidine, clausine L, mukonidine, glycosini ne, mukonal, 
and clausine V via AuClAcatalyzed cyclization of in dolyA2,3A
